title: WASSCE Further Maths: Calculus (Differentiation & Integration) - Further Mathematics - Rates of Change
subject: Further Mathematics

questions.q: A spherical balloon is deflating such that its volume decreases at a constant rate of $10 \text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$. Find the rate of change of its radius when the radius is $5 \text{ cm}$.
questions.explain: The volume of a sphere is $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$. Differentiating gives $\frac{dV}{dr} = 4\pi r^2$. Using the chain rule, $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dr} \times \frac{dr}{dt}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = -10$ (decreasing) and $r = 5$, we have $-10 = 4\pi(5)^2 \times \frac{dr}{dt} \implies -10 = 100\pi \times \frac{dr}{dt}$. Thus, $\frac{dr}{dt} = -\frac{1}{10\pi} \text{ cm/s}$.
questions.subject: Further Mathematics

questions.q: A circular metal plate expands when heated such that its radius increases at a constant rate of $0.02 \text{ cm/s}$. Find the exact rate of increase of its area when the radius is $10 \text{ cm}$.
questions.explain: The area $A$ of a circle is $\pi r^2$. Differentiating with respect to time $t$ gives $\frac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r \cdot \frac{dr}{dt}$. Substituting $r = 10$ and $\frac{dr}{dt} = 0.02$ yields $\frac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi(10)(0.02) = 0.4\pi \text{ cm}^2/\text{s}$.
questions.subject: Further Mathematics

questions.q: Water is poured into a cylindrical container of radius $5\text{ cm}$ at the constant rate of $50\pi \text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$. Find the rate at which the water level is rising.
questions.explain: The volume of a cylinder is $V = \pi r^2 h$. Since the radius is constant at $r = 5$, $V = 25\pi h$. Differentiating with respect to time yields $\frac{dV}{dt} = 25\pi \frac{dh}{dt}$. Given that $\frac{dV}{dt} = 50\pi$, we set up $50\pi = 25\pi \frac{dh}{dt}$, resulting in $\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{50\pi}{25\pi} = 2 \text{ cm/s}$.

questions.q: Sand falls to form a conical pile such that the radius of the base is always equal to its height. If the volume of the pile is increasing at a rate of $3 \text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$, find the rate at which the height is increasing when the height is $2 \text{ cm}$.
questions.explain: The volume of a cone is $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$. Since $r = h$, $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi h^3$. Differentiating with respect to time $t$ gives $\frac{dV}{dt} = \pi h^2 \frac{dh}{dt}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = 3$ and $h = 2$, we have $3 = \pi(2)^2 \frac{dh}{dt} = 4\pi \frac{dh}{dt}$. Therefore, $\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{3}{4\pi} \text{ cm/s}$.
questions.subject: Further Mathematics

questions.q: A hollow right circular cone with vertex downwards has a semi-vertical angle of $30^{\circ}$. Water is poured into the cone at a constant rate of $5 \text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$. At what rate is the depth of the water rising when it is $3 \text{ cm}$ deep?
questions.explain: The radius $r$ relates to the depth $h$ by $r = h \tan 30^{\circ} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$. The volume $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi \left(\frac{h}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 h = \frac{\pi}{9}h^3$. Differentiating, $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{\pi}{3}h^2 \frac{dh}{dt}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = 5$ and $h=3$, we get $5 = \frac{\pi}{3}(3)^2 \frac{dh}{dt} = 3\pi \frac{dh}{dt}$, resulting in $\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{5}{3\pi} \text{ cm/s}$.
questions.subject: Further Mathematics

questions.q: The length of each edge of a cube is increasing at a uniform rate of $0.5 \text{ cm/s}$. Find the rate at which the volume is increasing when the edge length is $4 \text{ cm}$.
questions.explain: Volume of a cube $V = s^3$. Differentiating with respect to time $t$ gives $\frac{dV}{dt} = 3s^2 \frac{ds}{dt}$. Substitute $s = 4$ and $\frac{ds}{dt} = 0.5$: $\frac{dV}{dt} = 3(4)^2(0.5) = 3(16)(0.5) = 24 \text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$.
